state: Assess the remaining CanStats design boundary. The implemented-language draft currently specifies analytics writes but not reads; there is no deployed implementation. Typed bound capabilities already express asynchronous service calls with caller delegation and completion/result records. Stats keeps authoritative accepted-event identities and exact visitor/session summaries in D1 while sending nonidentifying dimensions to Analytics Engine. Weighted breakdowns, disclosure-safe health and explicit partial/estimated results are actual app requirements. The official provider guidance requires each row's _sample_interval for weighted counts via sum; multiplying by one uniform factor is wrong. This work may edit contracts/examples only, not create compiler/runtime/provider code. Goals include compact first-class Cloudflare use, a canonical path per primitive and avoidance of compensating scaffolding. One proposal uses a finite DimensionsV1.read(site,UTC bounds,dimension,configured goals) contract mapped to the declared dataset. Results expose at most200 keys plus full denominators,sampled/complete flags,time; private caller projections validate correlation and output, ignore superseded completions and expire, with polling only rereading them. This reuses current mechanisms but authors another app-specific report contract. Another proposal makes aggregate reads a standard schema-derived surface of analytics bindings with those same authority/asynchrony/coverage guarantees. That adds shared language-service design now and may remove repeated wrappers later. Weighted results never supply distinct people/session sums or prove paid sales.

read_boundary.instructions: Choose the more proportionate location for aggregate-read semantics under these requirements and existing mechanisms.

criteria.app_capability: Use the already specified capability mechanism for one constrained Stats report adapter. Its manual schemas/projections keep the present design bounded and explicit, at the cost of application text and possible later commonization.
criteria.shared_analytics: Extend the existing analytics service surface with a schema-derived typed aggregate query contract. This centralizes repeated read logic and improves first-class authoring while expanding shared design work for authorization, queued reads and estimates.
